note: Read 2026-11-01 at the owner's word ("Continue on to the rest of layer 4"): the unions' and guilds' rules that read a person's legal and professional names (professional-name uniqueness, credit names and pseudonyms), how one joins each and what it costs, and the rule that a performer be authorised to work where the job is. One research subagent; every quote checked by the lead against its saved page.

figures.finding: SAG-AFTRA aims that no member uses a professional name the same as, or so close as to be confused with, another member's; a joiner gives three alternate names, availability is settled only when the initiation fee is paid, and a member may still use their own legal name if they sign an Acknowledgement form.
figures.applies: SAG-AFTRA (United States), help-centre answer updated 2024-04-03, read 2026-11-01.
figures.use: When a life joins SAG-AFTRA with a billing name a current member holds, the game asks for another (up to three choices) unless the billing name is the player's own legal name, which it allows after an acknowledgement.

sources.said: It is SAG-AFTRA's objective that no member uses a professional name which is the same as, or resembles so closely as to tend to be confused with the name of any other member.

During the joining process, the actor/performer will be asked for three alternate name choices, in case the first choice is not available. A final name-availability check is done at the time the initiation fee is paid.

SAG-AFTRA cannot preclude a member from using their legal name as their professional name. When such a situation arises, SAG-AFTRA requires that the applicant/member sign an "Acknowledgement" form in order for their request to be processed.
In the case of a member on Honorable Withdrawal status or Suspended Payment Owing status from the union, the professional name is available after a period of 5 years.

figures.finding: Equity (UK) gives each member a protected Equity name that no other joiner may take if it is the same or sounds alike; shortened forms, sound-alike spellings, plural surnames, a middle initial, Jr./Sr. and Mc/Mac do not distinguish, while an O' prefix, a double-barrelled surname or a middle name do; a joiner offers three options, and changing an Equity name costs £32 (free with a legal name change).

value.protected: while a member and up to 12 months after death

figures.applies: Equity (United Kingdom), page read 2026-11-01.
figures.use: Joining Equity with a billing name that matches or sounds like a current member's (by these tests) is refused and the player picks another of three; the game has no legal-name exception here.

sources.said: This Equity name is protected while you are a member, meaning that no other person can join Equity with the same or similar-sounding name as you.

Equity does not allow members to have the same or similar-sounding names. The following are NOT sufficient to distinguish you from other artists: Example Shortened forms of names Stewart/Stewie/Stu or Rebecca/Becky/Bex Names that are spelled differently but sound the same Judi/Judy or Smith/Smyth Pluralised surnames Oliver Well/Oliver Wells A middle initial Ruby L Klein/Ruby Klein The addition of Senior or Junior Joseph Carroll/Joseph Carroll Jr. Surnames beginning Mc or Mac are treated the same Macbeth/McBeth

The following ARE sufficient to distinguish you from other artists: Example O' at the beginning of the name O'Malley/Malley Double-barrelled surname or middle name John Smith-Jones/John Matthew Smith/John Smith
When making your application please give three distinct options for your Equity name in case your first and second name choices are not available.
The fee for changing your Equity name is £32. There is no charge if you are also changing legal name.

figures.finding: ACTRA requires an applicant whose name is identical to an existing member's to change their professional or stage name before being accepted; adding a first or middle initial is not enough.

value.identical_name: must change professional/stage name before acceptance

figures.applies: ACTRA National By-Laws, By-Law No. 1, Section IV, document dated June 25, 2026.
figures.use: A billing name identical to a current ACTRA member's (initials ignored) must change before the life becomes an ACTRA member.

sources.said: An applicant for membership with a name identical to that of an existing member shall adopt a change of professional/stage name before being accepted.
The addition of a first and/or middle initial to an otherwise identical name shall not be considered a sufficient change.

figures.finding: Canadian Actors' Equity makes changing one's professional name a condition of membership where it conflicts with an existing artist's name.

value.conflict: must change professional name as a condition of membership

figures.applies: CAEA Bylaws, bylaw 4, bylaws last amended March 30, 2026.
figures.use: A billing name in conflict with an existing CAEA artist's must change before the life joins CAEA.

sources.said: As a condition of membership, an artist shall be required to change their professional name where there is a conflict with the name of an existing artist.

figures.finding: Actors' Equity Association (US) registers the applicant's signature as their professional name and will not enrol an applicant under, nor let a member use, a name the same as or confusingly like an existing member's, unless the existing member consents or the National Council finds no likelihood of confusion or extenuating circumstances; violating it is a disciplinary offence.

exceptions: National Council finding of no likelihood of confusion or extenuating circumstances

figures.applies: AEA By-Laws Article 9 Section 7, PDF dated 2023-04-27, read 2026-11-01.
figures.use: A conflicting billing name is refused at AEA unless the holder consents (a contact the life knows) or the Council finds no confusion.

sources.said: The Association shall not enroll an applicant under a name nor shall a member use a name professionally which is the same as or resembles so closely as to tend to be confused with, the name of an existing enrolled member, except that an applicant may enroll under and use such name professionally upon proof of consent by the existing member, or a finding by the National Council that under the circum- stances there is no likelihood of confusion or that there are extenuating circumstances.

figures.finding: Under the WGA MBA a writer entitled to screen credit who was paid or guaranteed less than $200,000 for the picture may take credit under a reasonable pseudonym, chosen within five business days after credits are final, with no loss of rights; the pseudonym must first be registered with the Guild and may not duplicate another writer's name or pseudonym or a public figure's name.

value.registration: written notice to the Membership Department with Social Security number, if any

figures.applies: WGA Screen Credits Manual (theatrical), read 2026-11-01.
figures.use: A writer life paid under $200,000 on a film may take its writing credit under a registered pseudonym (not matching another writer or a public figure) within five business days of final credits.

sources.said: any writer who is entitled to credit on the screen and who has been paid (or is guaranteed payment of) less than two hundred thousand dollars ($200,000) for writing services or literary materials relating to the particular motion picture shall have the right to be accorded credit on the screen, in advertising or otherwise, in a reasonable pseudonymous name. A writer must exercise this right within five (5) business days after final determination of writing credits.

Before using a pseudonym a writer must register it with the Guild by sending a written notice to the Membership Department with the writer's Social Security number, if any. A pseudonym may not duplicate the name or pseudonym of another writer or the name of a public figure.

figures.finding: Under the DGA Basic Agreement, when another director on the picture has the same first and last name, the Guild decides whether the credit must carry the middle name or middle initial.

value.same_first_and_last_name: Guild decides whether credit adds middle name or middle initial

figures.finding: The PGA's Producers Mark, once licensed, is placed immediately next to the producer's name in the credit ("Jane Smith, p.g.a."), not after another mark or a combined credit; PGA membership is not required for it.

figures.finding: SAG-AFTRA membership opens after one day as a principal or speaking performer, three days as a background actor under a SAG-AFTRA agreement, or one paid-up year in a sister union (ACTRA, AEA, AGMA, AGVA) with one paid principal job; eligibility does not expire and ultra-low-budget, student and short films do not count.
figures.applies: SAG-AFTRA help answer updated 2023-11-21.

Performers may join SAG-AFTRA if the applicant is a paid-up member of an affiliated performers' union such as ACTRA, AEA, AGMA or AGVA for a period of one year, and has worked and been paid for at least once as a principal performer in that union’s jurisdiction.
1. Eligibility does not expire. 2. Ultra Low Budget, Student, or Short Films do not qualify towards SAG-AFTRA eligibility, but may create a pathway to join.

sources.title: SAG-AFTRA Help: Professional Name Availability
sources.said: It is SAG-AFTRA's objective that no member uses a professional name which is the same as, or resembles so closely as to tend to be confused with the name of any other member. … During the joining process, the actor/performer will be asked for three alternate name choices, in case the first choice is not available. A final name-availability check is done at the time the initiation fee is paid. … SAG-AFTRA cannot preclude a member from using their legal name as their professional name. When such a situation arises, SAG-AFTRA requires that the applicant/member sign an "Acknowledgement" form in order for their request to be processed. … In the case of a member on Honorable Withdrawal status or Suspended Payment Owing status from the union, the professional name is available after a period of 5 years.

sources.title: Equity Name: What You Need to Know
sources.said: This Equity name is protected while you are a member, meaning that no other person can join Equity with the same or similar-sounding name as you. … Equity does not allow members to have the same or similar-sounding names. The following are NOT sufficient to distinguish you from other artists: Example Shortened forms of names Stewart/Stewie/Stu or Rebecca/Becky/Bex Names that are spelled differently but sound the same Judi/Judy or Smith/Smyth Pluralised surnames Oliver Well/Oliver Wells A middle initial Ruby L Klein/Ruby Klein The addition of Senior or Junior Joseph Carroll/Joseph Carroll Jr. Surnames beginning Mc or Mac are treated the same Macbeth/McBeth … The following ARE sufficient to distinguish you from other artists: Example O' at the beginning of the name O'Malley/Malley Double-barrelled surname or middle name John Smith-Jones/John Matthew Smith/John Smith … When making your application please give three distinct options for your Equity name in case your first and second name choices are not available. … The fee for changing your Equity name is £32. There is no charge if you are also changing legal name.

sources.said: The Association shall not enroll an applicant under a name nor shall a member use a name professionally which is the same as or resembles so closely as to tend to be confused with, the name of an existing enrolled member, except that an applicant may enroll under and use such name professionally upon proof of consent by the existing member, or a finding by the National Council that under the circum- stances there is no likelihood of confusion or that there are extenuating circumstances. … (a) The initiation fee shall be $1800, effective January 1, 2022.

sources.title: WGA Screen Credits Manual
sources.said: any writer who is entitled to credit on the screen and who has been paid (or is guaranteed payment of) less than two hundred thousand dollars ($200,000) for writing services or literary materials relating to the particular motion picture shall have the right to be accorded credit on the screen, in advertising or otherwise, in a reasonable pseudonymous name. A writer must exercise this right within five (5) business days after final determination of writing credits. … Before using a pseudonym a writer must register it with the Guild by sending a written notice to the Membership Department with the writer's Social Security number, if any. A pseudonym may not duplicate the name or pseudonym of another writer or the name of a public figure.

sources.title: SAG-AFTRA Help: What is a Taft-Hartley Report?
sources.said: A Taft-Hartley report is a form provided by the Union to Producers in order notify the Union of any hiring of non-union performers. A Producer must submit the Taft-Hartley report within 15 days from the performer's initial work date.
